4. The defendants (petitioners herein) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the allegations made in the plaint and contended that the suit was barred by limitation, waiver, estopple and acquiescence. It was further contended that the mortgage deed in question in fact was out and out a sale deed, that is, conditional sale and that the transaction was past and closed and thus the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 12. The suit was instituted for redemption of mortgage. On perusal of deed of mortgage, exhibit-1 it appears that it was registered on 10.6.1937 corresponding to 27th Jaistha, 1344 B.S. In the recital of the said deed it has been mentioned that the predecessors of the plaintiffs took loan of Tk. 119 at the rate of 2% interest from Panaullah Khan, the predecessor of the defendants mortgaging the suit land with a condition that they would re-pay the loan money within 7(seven) years, that is, by 27th Jaistha, 1351 B.S. corresponding to 10.6.1944. On re-payment of loan money with interest within the stipulated period the said Panaullah Khan would return the mortgaged land. As the mortgage was an complete usufractuary mortgage, the loan money with interest was repaid by the usufructs of the mortgaged land, On the refusal of the defendants to return the mortgaged land in the first part of Jaistha, 1393 B.S., the plaintiffs instituted the suit on 15.2.1987 for redemption of mortgage under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 15. The Appellate Division in another case of Asmat Ali Vs. Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 while dealing with sections 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 held that President's Order No.88 of 1972 created a special forum for restoration of mortgaged property. But it did not take away any right of redemption available to a mortgagor by filing a mortgage suit. 

 "Apart from the provision of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and remedies under section 95 of the said Act, the remedy of civil Court is always available to the mortgagor in a case of mortgage, the limitation of which for redemption is within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption and a suit can be filed for redemption of the mortgage." 

 17. In view of the proposition of law settled by the Apex Court, as quoted above, and considering the evidence on record I am of the view that the transaction was a complete usufractuary mortgage and not an out and out sale and the plaintiffs being the heirs of the mortgagor have every right to redeem the mortgage by instituting the suit for redemption of mortgage under section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The suit is instituted on 15.2.1987, that is, well within the period of statutory period of limitation of 60 years under Article 148 of the Limitation Act, 1908 and hence the suit is quite maintainable.
